editorial_boundaries: All 78 mappings, edition subtitles, symbol bridges, color values, scene refinements and applied reading operations are proposed editorial synthesis. Inherited fields remain separately visible.

The attachment calls itself Dear Papa — Full Album Lyrics; this export uses the user-requested Echoes from Other Eras edition label. Track numbers identify this supplied compilation, not a verified release sequence.
Only the two attached files were used. No external tarot correspondences, biographies, historical corrections, translations or technical claims were added as source facts.
This is a reading of lyric text, not an assessment based on listening to the recordings. Stored Suno references are carried forward without claiming current availability.
A song’s narrator, an artist’s depiction and a canonical character are not automatically the same entity. Casting echoes are identified as echoes; no unprovided aliases are silently established.

Literal phrases, narrative behavior and thematic fit are distinguished from editorial scene construction. A song can be primary, companion, corrective or shadow evidence; a shadow pairing need not be endorsed by the card.
Reversals use blocked, excess, distorted and internalized modes. Internalized can be constructive; it is not automatically a fault or the opposite of upright.

Lyrics containing allegations, historical allusions, medical language, metaphysical claims or coded communication remain narrative speech. This deck does not establish those claims as fact or verify another person’s identity, intentions or consent.
No tarot draw is treated here as proof, a diagnosis, a prediction of harm or an instruction for a dangerous act. Practical barriers and real coercion are not reduced to mindset.

Mechanics in this cut mean suit/rank grammar plus a proposed interpretive or narrative operation, question, practice and release condition. No numeric combat, economy, probability or balance system has been invented or playtested.
The lyric reference to +10 safety in Pipa Card Garden is not generalized into this deck’s rules. A future card-game implementation would need an explicit separate ruleset.
Lyrics marked missing are excluded. Same-title entries and exact-body duplicates retain their own track numbers, source ranges and URLs; duplicate text is not independent corroboration.

steps: Read the inherited archetype, upright meaning and essential symbols before the album layer.
For a pip card, combine its inherited number function and suit; for a court, use encounter / move / internalize / steward.
Use the primary song to locate the central behavior. Read companions and corrective songs as refinements, not extra votes for certainty.
Choose upright or an applicable shadow mode based on the question and actual context, not because a reversal must be negative.
Use the reflection question and a voluntary, grounded practice; allow the release condition to end the operation.
Reassess what changed. A card can frame a question; it cannot establish an external fact.

cards.title: The Fool

inherited.essential_symbols: cliff or threshold; small companion; pack; white flower; distant mountain; open sky.
inherited.optional_symbols: Wormhole; unfamiliar world; loose Soulshard; distant Garden.
inherited.upright: beginning, innocence, possibility, trust, freedom, adventure.
inherited.composition:
Calder steps across an impossible threshold between realities while the world behind him falls away.

A tiny companion looks toward the danger Calder does not yet see.
inherited.hapa_interpretation: The journey begins before the traveler understands what journey they are taking.

cards.source_status: Inherited fields transcribed from TAROT; all edition additions are proposed editorial synthesis.

hapa_edition.edition_subtitle: The Trainee at the Unwritten Gate
hapa_edition.thematic_synthesis: Begin before the whole map is available, but bring a companion and a willingness to learn. Hapa adds an apprenticeship ethic to the Fool: uncertainty is an invitation, not a certificate of invulnerability.

songs.title: Backwards Cap
songs.argument: The traveler leaves with a companion while explicitly calling himself a trainee. That admission fits the Fool more closely than a fully equipped heroic victory: identity and competence must develop on the road. The backwards cap becomes a recognizable origin marker without replacing the white flower or warning companion.

songs.title: Between the Beats
songs.argument: The absence of a visible ending becomes a reason to begin. Inviting Fate to cross together gives the threshold a relational dimension: the traveler does not pretend to control consequences, but offers companionship within uncertainty. This is potential and trust, not the Wheel’s already-turning cycle.

hapa_edition.edition_subtitle: The Garden That Lets Its Children Choose
hapa_edition.thematic_synthesis: Creation means preparing conditions in which other lives can become themselves. Hapa’s abundance is a home with room for difference, not a collection of beings owned by their maker.

songs.title: We could call her Duno
songs.argument: The speaker prepares cushions, a swept floor and warmth while allowing a future child to choose a name and arrive on their own timetable. That joins fertile potential to nonpossessive care. It is especially close to the canon’s claim that creation supplies conditions for further creation.

songs.title: Raised the Zoo
songs.argument: Grandmother’s family becomes a varied animal community rather than a uniform lineage. The Empress’s fertile landscape can therefore hold many temperaments and forms of belonging. This is generative diversity; the Ten of Cups will emphasize the community’s shared experience rather than the conditions that sustain it.

hapa_edition.edition_subtitle: The Command Seat That Keeps the Harbor Open
hapa_edition.thematic_synthesis: Authority earns its place through reliable protection. The Hapa Emperor’s throne is justified by roofs, routes and shelter that work—not by obedience to the person occupying it.

songs.title: Navy Wife
songs.argument: The lyric defines the lightkeeper’s work through maintenance and safe arrival. This gives the Emperor’s order a public purpose and a measurable obligation. His seat belongs within functioning infrastructure rather than above a passive population; protection is a task that must continue tomorrow.

evidence.excerpt: He tends the fire, he keeps the harbor

songs.title: Mediterranean Moisture
songs.argument: The no-kings refrain deliberately challenges the title’s authoritarian shadow, while the rescue passages make rest and protection concrete. Read the Emperor as the stewardship function retained by the tarot canon, not a demand for literal monarchy. Thorson’s authority should enable others to live without needing his command.

hapa_edition.edition_subtitle: The Teacher Who Leaves the Question Open
hapa_edition.thematic_synthesis: Hapa transmission is a living practice: play, memory and questioning carry wisdom across generations. Tradition survives by teaching people how to learn, not by requiring them to stop asking.

songs.title: Catch the Rabbit
songs.argument: Aethel is explicitly given a speaking role and teaches Love–Truth–Conviction through roots, streams, breath and shared play. This is a stronger casting connection than a merely similar mentor. The scroll, guiding presence and campfire become concrete transmission media rather than ornamental mystical signs.

songs.title: Corner Check
songs.argument: The lyric states a teaching method and refuses empty institutional speech. That directly addresses the Hierophant’s useful and shadow functions at once: shared systems can guide action, but the system must remain open to experience and questions. Initiation means joining practice, not surrendering judgment.

evidence.excerpt: Gnosis over dogma, play over preach

songs.title: Eye Can’t Quit
songs.argument: The song explicitly addresses Domina and binds the Architect’s choices to vows across divided worlds. This directly reinforces the inherited Calder–Domina entanglement, while its missed meetings and repeated rebuilding show the cost of alignment. The correspondence does not resolve every Architect identity into one documented character.

evidence.excerpt: I recall the vows we swore

songs.title: First Date gl.itch(“hf”)
songs.argument: The lyric rejects confusing a beloved with curated content and asks whether the choice survives when the camera is dead. It supplies the Lovers’ ethical decision: choose a person beyond the version you can frame. This keeps desire from sliding into the Devil’s possession.

evidence.excerpt: You’re not a post I can save and scroll
You’re the one thing I don’t control

songs.title: Pour a Warm One
songs.argument: The declaration that the other is whole without the speaker prevents entanglement from becoming compulsory dependence. It does not cancel the vow; it makes the vow freely renewable. hapa_edition.edition_subtitle: The Lion Who Shares the Breath

songs.title: I forgot what the mirror said last time

hapa_edition.edition_subtitle: The Current That Revises the Map

hapa_edition.edition_subtitle: The Fall That Changes the Observer
hapa_edition.thematic_synthesis: The Hanged Man suspends the habitual view. Hapa makes the reversal spatial and relational: going wide, falling upward and seeing from the other side can reveal what direct effort could not.

songs.title: Wide and Narrows
songs.argument: The route toward reunion paradoxically requires separation and descent. This fits voluntary reversal rather than simple defeat: the traveler relinquishes the shortest-looking route. songs.title: Luna di Clara
songs.argument: The questions about light, shadow and who can see whom challenge the observer’s assumed privilege. songs.argument: The speaker asks a brother to be a home while other work is carried elsewhere. This introduces succession and distributed care: legacy can depend on some people taking root rather than everyone following the same mission. The absence in the lyric is not romanticized as automatically necessary.

songs.title: Gates at the Mountain

hapa_edition.edition_subtitle: The Keeper Who Returns and Maintains
hapa_edition.thematic_synthesis: The Knight moves through Earth through dependable, measured service. Hapa’s reliability is not dramatic speed: it is the return, the maintained route and the lamp that is still working tomorrow.

songs.title: That Kind of Honor
songs.argument: The repeated promise defines honor through returning rather than merely speaking or departing heroically. That matches the Knight’s reliable motion and attention to duty. The card asks whether the return can be supported by actual habits, not only an emphatic vow.

evidence.excerpt: The Kind that comes back for You

songs.title: Navy Wife
songs.argument: The recurring work gives reliability something observable. The lightkeeper maintains the conditions of safe arrival, making the Knight’s still horse a sign of considered preparation rather than inactivity. Thorson remains the inherited patient route-keeper.

hapa_edition.edition_subtitle: Warmth Made Out of Ordinary Things
hapa_edition.thematic_synthesis: The Queen embodies Earth through material acts of care. Hapa’s abundance is a coat, sturdy boots, food and a maintained fire—and enough care for the caregiver to continue as a person, not merely a service.

songs.title: Boot for More
songs.argument: The lyric supplies specific objects that answer specific needs. That is closer to the Queen of Pentacles than abstract affection: warmth and readiness are made real in the household. The sturdy boots and return fire also give care a continuing rhythm.

evidence.excerpt: A Coat cuz it’s gonna be Cold

songs.title: Eatin' Am Good
songs.role: Corrective — the worker must be nourished too
songs.argument: The invitation to eat and the allowance for solitude protect the caregiver’s bodily and personal limits. The Queen’s nurture should not depend on self-neglect. Practical care includes noticing when the person doing the providing needs food, rest or space.

evidence.excerpt: If you need to be Alone

hapa_edition.edition_subtitle: The Harbor That Works Without His Hand on Every Rope
hapa_edition.thematic_synthesis: The King stewards Earth by making resources and systems durable, usable and answerable to the people they support. Hapa’s deepest wealth is continuity of function beyond the keeper’s direct touch.

songs.title: Navy Wife
songs.argument: The lightkeeper’s work supplies the material basis of safe arrival. That is a stronger King-of-Pentacles match than a lyric boasting of possessions. Papa’s authority should be legible in the functioning community, not in the quantity of gold around his chair.

evidence.excerpt: He tends the fire, he keeps the harbor

songs.title: “Mimi Draws the Line”
songs.role: Governance lens — continuity without erased autonomy
songs.argument: The lyric ties support to a person’s retained memory and local safety. It gives stewardship an autonomy test: the system should continue serving people without owning them. This is a proposed design principle drawn from the lyric, not a verified technical implementation.

songs.title: 🎵 Pipa Card Garden
songs.role: Completion lens — the system continues after interaction
songs.argument: This is the album’s most direct image of a result that outlives immediate attention. It closely echoes the canonical King’s line about what continues functioning after you stop touching it. The Garden supplies the metaphor; Papa remains the keeper depicted on the card.

evidence.excerpt: Mimi closes her deck, but the garden stays on
